'''Bryna Rebekah Kra''' (born 1966) is an American mathematician and the Sarah Rebecca Roland Professor at [[Northwestern University]]. Kra served as the president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] from 2023 to 2025. She is a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[National Academy of Sciences]]. Her academic work centered on [[dynamical systems]] and [[ergodic theory]]. In particular Kra has made significant contributions to the structure theory of characteristic factors for multiple ergodic averages.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/bryna-kra-builds-mathematical-windows-to-symbolize-the-complex-20201117/|magazine=[[Quanta Magazine]]|title=Searching Symbols for the Rules of Change: Bryna Kra searches for the patterns in sequences of numbers that explain how complicated dynamical systems evolve over time|date=November 17, 2020|first=Rachel|last=Crowell}}</ref> This work has allowed her to address problems in [[number theory]] and [[combinatorics]].<ref>{{citation
 | last1 = Host | first1 = Bernard
 | last2 = Kra | first2 = Bryna
 | doi = 10.4007/annals.2005.161.397
 | issue = 1
 | journal = [[Annals of Mathematics]]
 | mr = 2150389
 | pages = 397–488
 | series = Second Series
 | title = Nonconventional ergodic averages and nilmanifolds
 | url = http://www.math.northwestern.edu/~kra/papers/convnil.pdf
 | volume = 161
 | year = 2005| doi-access = free
 }}.</ref>

==Education and career==
Kra was born in 1966 in [[Boston]].<ref>{{citation|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|page=942|volume=62|issue=8|date=September 2015|title=Bryna Kra|department=Biographies of Candidates 2015|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201508/rnoti-p931a.pdf#page=12 }}</ref> She graduated with a bachelor's degree from [[Harvard University]] in 1988, and obtained her Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1995 under the guidance of [[Yitzhak Katznelson]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=39209}}</ref> She held postdoctoral positions at the [[Hebrew University]] in Jerusalem, the [[University of Michigan]], the [[Institut des hautes études scientifiques|IHÉS]] and the [[Ohio State University]] before joining the mathematics faculty at [[Pennsylvania State University]] as an assistant professor. Since 2004 Kra has been a professor of mathematics at [[Northwestern University]], where she was department chair from 2009 to 2012.

==Book==
With Bernard Host, Kra is the author of the book ''Nilpotent Structures in Ergodic Theory'' ([[Mathematical Surveys and Monographs]] 236, [[American Mathematical Society]], 2018).

==Honors==
In 2010  Kra was awarded the [[Levi L. Conant Prize]] for her expository article "The [[Green–Tao theorem]] on arithmetic progressions in the primes: an ergodic point of view".<ref>{{citation
 | last = Kra | first = Bryna
 | doi = 10.1090/S0273-0979-05-01086-4
 | issue = 1
 | journal = Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society
 | mr = 2188173
 | pages = 3–23
 | series = New Series
 | title = The Green-Tao theorem on arithmetic progressions in the primes: an ergodic point of view
 | volume = 43
 | year = 2006| doi-access = free
 }}</ref><ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201004/rtx100400515p.pdf|title=2010 Conant Prize|journal= Notices of the American Mathematical Society|date=April 2010|pages=515–516|volume=57|issue=4}}.</ref> In 2006 she was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Madrid]] ("From combinatorics to ergodic theory and back again"),<ref name="2006 ICM Bryna Kra">{{cite web |author-last=Kra | author-first=Bryna |title=''In:''Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians (Madrid, August 22-30, 2006) (Volume III Invited Lectures) |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM2006.3/ICM2006.3.ocr.pdf | access-date=2024-01-07}}</ref> and was named an AMS Centennial Fellow the same year.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200606/people.pdf|journal= Notices of the American Mathematical Society|department=Mathematics People|title=2006–2007 AMS Centennial Fellowships Awarded|page=686|first=Allyn|last=Jackson|volume=53|issue=6|date=June–July 2006}}.</ref> In 2012 she became a fellow of the American Mathematical Society.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society], retrieved 2013-07-07.</ref> In 2016 she became a fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amacad.org/content/members/newFellows.aspx?s=c|title=Newly Elected Members|date=April 2016|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|access-date=2016-04-20}}</ref> In 2019, she was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430143122/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 30, 2019|work=News from the National Academy of Sciences|title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and Foreign Associates; Historic Number of Women Elected to Its Membership|date=April 30, 2019}}</ref> She was named a 2021 [[Simons Foundation|Simons Fellows]] in Mathematics.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-02-04|title=2021 Simons Fellows in Mathematics and Theoretical Physics Announced|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/2021/02/04/2021-simons-fellows-in-mathematics-and-theoretical-physics-announced/|access-date=2021-07-18|website=Simons Foundation|language=en-US}}</ref>  Kra was elected to the 2023 class of fellows of the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] "for her vision and work creating programs to support women in mathematics, especially GROW (Graduate Research Opportunities for Women) and AWM student chapters; for her leadership in the mathematics community, including serving on the AWM Executive Committee and serving as president of AMS; and for making advocacy for women a priority throughout her career."<ref name="AWMfellow">{{cite web |title=The AWM Fellows Program: 2023 Class of AWM Fellows |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-fellows/2023-awm-fellows/ |publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics |access-date=23 October 2022}}</ref> Kra was elected president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2021 and she served as president from February 2023 to January 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ams.org/news?class_id=1&expand=1&type=news|title=Kra Takes Helm of AMS Presidency|publisher=American Mathematical Society|access-date=10 April 2023}}</ref>

==Family relations==
Kra is the daughter of mathematician [[Irwin Kra]].<ref>[http://www.mathforamerica.org/about/board/irwin-kra Irwin Kra] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160806221605/http://www.mathforamerica.org/about/board/irwin-kra |date=2016-08-06 }}, [[Math for America]] board, retrieved 2016-06-24.</ref>
